Q4: "In this case, the individual presented with a half-year history of pain in different parts of their body, and the pain gradually worsened, causing difficulty in walking and moving their shoulders."

Parent requirement likely involves: first case (from two cases in 2010s about disorder) was reported in a country; that country is largest country of its dominant religion in world at time of establishment; in this case individual had half-year history of pain in different parts of body, pain gradually worsened, causing difficulty walking and moving shoulders.

Current Claims include C7: "A case report of FOP described a 10-year-old Pakistani boy who presented with a 6-month history of pain and tender masses on the back, left arm, and left hip; the pain was insidious, gradually worsened, and caused difficulty walking and decreased range of motion of the shoulders and hips."

C7 appears to establish the clinical presentation for a FOP case in Pakistani boy: half-year (6-month) history, pain in different parts (back, left arm, left hip), gradually worsened, difficulty walking and decreased range of motion of shoulders/hips. So Q4 part is supported by C7 (assuming this is the first case). However Q3: country = Pakistan? Largest country of its dominant religion in the world at time of establishment? Pakistan is not largest Muslim country by population? At time of establishment? Pakistan established 1947, largest Muslim country? Actually Indonesia is largest Muslim population. But "largest country of its dominant religion" might mean "country that is largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment" = Pakistan was created as largest Muslim state? Hmm. But we don't need solve. Need residual objective inside R3. Since Q4 seems supported by C7, but Q3 not yet established by claims. Claims mention Pakistani boy (C7), but does that establish "first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment"? C7 says Pakistani boy; implies case reported in Pakistan? It says a case report described a 10-year-old Pakistani boy. That may establish individual is Pakistani, not necessarily country where case was reported. It could be reported in another country. Also need relation: country was largest country of its dominant religion in world at time of establishment. No claim about Pakistan being largest Muslim country at establishment. So residual likely: establish that the country where the first case was reported (or the relevant country associated with first case) was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment. But also maybe need establish that the first case was reported in Pakistan? C7 has Pakistani boy but not explicitly "reported in Pakistan". However C7 says "A case report ... described a 10-year-old Pakistani boy..." That could support nationality but not report location. Need local residual one coherent part.

Parent Requirement has two conditions: Q3 and Q4. Q4 maybe already established by C7. Q3 remains. So local_residual: "The country where the first case was reported (the case with the 6-month pain history) was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." We need preserve uncertainty. Use claims C7 as used because it supports Q4 and identifies Pakistani boy. But if we're only asking Q3 residual, we can cite C7 maybe to link first case? The used_claims field should list claims used to establish what's already done or context. Since C7 supports Q4, used_claims ["C7"]. The local_residual should be one objective. Mode residual.

Need be careful: "If some part already established by Claims, do not ask to establish that part again." So we ask Q3 part. Is Q3 a single coherent evidence objective? "The first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." This is a relational composite: country of first case, dominant religion, largest country, time of establishment. But it's one coherent objective: establish the country of first case meets that description. Could be one residual. Alternatively if first case country not established, we might ask "Identify the country where the first case was reported." That is a prerequisite for Q3. But Q3 mentions country and property. Should we ask the whole Q3? Parent requirement is R3 combining both. Since Q4 is supported by C7, residual is Q3. The residual can be "Establish the country in which the first case was reported and that it was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." But that bundles identifying country and establishing property. Is that okay? It's one coherent objective about the country property. However if country identity is not established, maybe we should not jump to property? The instruction: "Do not jump to a downstream attribute whose referent still needs to be established." If the country referent still needs to be established, maybe local residual should be "the country in which the first case was reported" rather than its attribute. But the Parent Requirement itself includes the country's attribute. We need identify one coherent evidence objective inside R3. The referent (country) may be unknown. We can ask to establish the country where the first case was reported. But that is only part of Q3. Then later its attribute. Which is better? Let's assess.

Original question: "The first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." This is a condition on the first case. To establish it, need know (a) which case is first; (b) country of report; (c) that country is largest country of its dominant religion at establishment. C7 says a 10-year-old Pakistani boy. That may imply country = Pakistan? But "Pakistani boy" doesn't necessarily mean reported in Pakistan. It could be reported elsewhere. Also "first case" relative to two cases in 2010s. C7 likely is the first case? C7 has 10-year-old Pakistani boy with 6-month history etc. C9 is the other case (16-year-old male, upper back pain/swelling, biopsy two months earlier, age 9 stiffness). So first case probably C7. Thus country is likely Pakistan. But claim doesn't explicitly say reported in Pakistan. However it says Pakistani boy, which strongly suggests Pakistan? But "reported in a country" could be inferred? Yet only Verified Claims count; C7 doesn't state report location. So residual could be: "Establish that the first case (the 10-year-old with 6-month pain) was reported in Pakistan." But then also Q3 says that country was largest country of dominant religion at time of establishment. Is that supported? No. Maybe we can ask one objective: "Establish the country in which the first FOP case was reported and whether that country was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." But that's two things. However it's a single relation: the country of report satisfies property. The referent may be known from C7 as Pakistani boy? Hmm.

The instruction says "If several independent unresolved parts remain, choose exactly ONE coherent part. Do not bundle independent research objectives." Is "identify country" and "establish its religious-largest status" independent? They are nested; establishing property requires country. Could be one compound condition. But we can choose one: the attribute (largest country of dominant religion at establishment) given country? But if country not established, that's jumping. The safer residual: "the country in which the first case was reported" as exploratory objective. But then we'd ignore Q3's attribute, which may be unresolved. However the prompt says "If no substantive part of the Parent Requirement is supported yet, still choose one faithful, low-commitment facet". Here Q4 supported, Q3 not. We can choose the country of report as facet of Q3. But Q3 also includes the property. We could phrase local_residual: "Establish the country where the first case (the case with the 6-month history of pain and difficulty walking/moving shoulders) was reported, as the parent requirement identifies that country via its status as the largest country of its dominant religion at establishment." That identifies one coherent objective: country of report. But the parent requirement's condition is not just country, but property. Hmm.

Let's examine "local_residual" definition: "one coherent evidence objective inside the Parent Requirement that still needs to be established now." It can be "the country in which the first case was reported" or "that the country of the first case was the largest country of its dominant religion at establishment." Which is more faithful? The Parent Requirement includes both Q3 and Q4. Q4 is established. The remaining unresolved part is Q3 entire. Q3 itself has two components: country of first case + property. But the property is relational to country. If we don't know country, we can ask to establish the country where the first case was reported. But that is only a sub-part of Q3, not Q3 entire. However the instruction says do not bundle independent parts. Country identity and property are not independent? They are related. But maybe we can ask the whole Q3 as one coherent objective: "Establish that the first case was reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion in the world at the time of its establishment." That's exactly the unresolved part, one sentence, one coherent condition. It doesn't bundle independent research objectives; it's the condition itself. The fact it has multiple semantic conditions doesn't mean we must split; it's one requirement. The prompt says Parent Requirement may contain more than one semantic condition; choose one coherent part. Q3 is one semantic condition? It has "reported in a country that was the largest country of its dominant religion..." It's one condition. Q4 is another. Since Q4 is supported, residual is Q3. So local_residual can be Q3 restated. That seems appropriate.

Need decide used_claims. Since C7 supports Q4, we include C7. But if local_residual is Q3, used_claims could be ["C7"] because it identifies the first case as 10-year-old Pakistani boy, providing partial context but not establishing Q3. The used_claims field likely should list claims that support already established parts. So yes.

Mode: residual.

Let's consider if C7 actually establishes Q4 fully. Q4: "In this case, the individual presented with a half-year history of pain in different parts of their body, and the pain gradually worsened, causing difficulty in walking and moving their shoulders." C7 says: 10-year-old Pakistani boy, 6-month history of pain and tender masses on back, left arm, left hip; pain insidious, gradually worsened, caused difficulty walking and decreased range of motion of shoulders and hips. This matches exactly: half-year (6-month), different parts (back, arm, hip), gradually worsened, difficulty walking and decreased range of motion of shoulders (moving shoulders). Yes, Q4 established for C7. So residual is Q3.

But is Q3 about "first case" or "the country" maybe already implied by Pakistani boy? The claim says Pakistani boy, which could imply the case was reported in Pakistan? Not necessarily. Also the property "largest country of its dominant religion in the world at time of establishment" is not in claims. So Q3 unresolved.

Thus final JSON.
